whatWorkedBest.pattern: Prediction giveaways tied to a huge real-world event
whatWorkedBest.evidence: The 3 World Cup Final prediction posts (5.4K-7.7K views) are still the single best organic format found on X to date.
whatWorkedBest.why: A live, massive, real-world moment everyone's already talking about, plus a low-effort way to participate (comment a guess) with a real, specific prize.

whatWorkedBest.pattern: Coordinated launch-day pushes (with ad spend behind them)
whatWorkedBest.evidence: The Aug 30 launch thread hit 8.0K reach on Instagram and 4.5K on X — the highest reach found in the internal Weekly Content Performance sheet. Marked "Ads Run" in the source data, so this isn't pure organic reach.
whatWorkedBest.why: Combining a real product change (new pricing) with paid promotion and a coordinated multi-post push clearly worked — but the ad spend is doing real work here, not just the content.

whatWorkedBest.evidence: "Meme / Relatable" is the top PURELY ORGANIC category in the internal sheet (939 avg reach), ahead of every other non-ads-run category.
whatWorkedBest.why: Low-effort-to-consume, funny, and not asking anything of the viewer — people engage without needing to care about pricing details.

whatWorkedLeast.evidence: Lowest-reach category in the internal sheet (235 avg) — confirms the same finding from the earlier X-only research pass (581 views there too). Two independent datasets now agree on this.
whatWorkedLeast.why: No hook, no incentive to engage — useful information but reads as a lesson, not a post.

whatWorkedLeast.evidence: LinkedIn averaged just 18 reach per post across 4 posts — by far the lowest of any platform, and 4 of the 5 lowest-performing posts overall in the entire dataset were on LinkedIn.
whatWorkedLeast.why: Likely an audience-fit problem more than a content problem — the same posts that do fine on X/IG are landing on an audience that isn't there for this content.

whatWorkedLeast.evidence: "Giveaway Winners" averaged 424 reach across 8 posts — solidly mid-to-low, well behind the giveaway ANNOUNCEMENT posts that preceded them (739 avg).
whatWorkedLeast.why: The announcement has the hook (a prize, a chance to win); the winner post is just closure — real but less inherently shareable.

recommendations: Lean further into prediction/giveaway formats tied to real, live cultural moments — not just trading news. GTA 6's Nov 19 launch is the next one of this scale.
Don't post educational content standalone — two independent datasets now agree this underperforms. Wrap the same information inside a giveaway, quiz, or meme format instead.
Re-evaluate LinkedIn's role — reposting the same content that works on X/IG isn't working there. Either build LinkedIn-native content or deprioritize it.

Separate ad-boosted performance from organic performance in future reporting — the Aug 30 launch numbers are real, but conflating "ads run" reach with organic reach overstates what content alone can do.
